answers.explanation: The CPU switches between jobs so often that users can interact with each one.
Timesharing is the logical extension: same switching idea, much faster, for interactive use.
Anything slower and interaction feels broken.
Each timesharing user has at least one process.
CPU scheduling picks which ready process runs next.
Swapping moves whole processes between memory and disk.
Virtual memory is one of the biggest topics later in the course.
Dozens of processes share the CPU, switched many times a second.
